source.title_on_document: Emergent Learner Agency in Implicit Human–AI Collaboration: How Supportive and Contrarian AI Personas Reshape Interaction

supplement.where: The paper mentions no online supplement. Appendix A (task text) and Appendix B (persona prompts) are inside this PDF, pp. 28-30.
supplement.holds: Nothing indicated. No arm-level means, SDs, or condition coefficients for the creativity outcome appear anywhere in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: 224 university students recruited on Prolific were randomly assigned at the triad level to 97 online triads: human-only control (30 groups of three humans), supportive-AI (33 groups of two humans plus an undisclosed GPT-5-based supportive teammate), or contrarian-AI (34 groups of two humans plus an undisclosed contrarian teammate). Each person wrote a 50-100 word sci-fi movie-plot synopsis alone, joined a 10-minute text chat to outline a plot, then wrote a revised synopsis alone without access to the chat or the baseline text. Creativity was scored as the change in Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI) from the pre to the post synopsis; most analyses concern discourse codes and self-reported cognitive load, teamwork satisfaction, and psychological safety.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Triad condition: human-only control, triad with an undisclosed supportive AI teammate, or triad with an undisclosed contrarian AI teammate
assignment.quote: Group allocation was randomised at the triad level into one of three experimental conditions
assignment.locator: p. 7, Section 3.1 Participants; also abstract p. 1 ('randomly assigned to 97 online triads') and Figure 2, p. 8

arms.name: Human-only Control
arms.description: 30 groups of three human participants; no AI in the chat

arms.name: Supportive-AI
arms.description: 33 groups of two humans and one undisclosed AI teammate with an affiliative, consensus-oriented persona

arms.name: Contrarian-AI
arms.description: 34 groups of two humans and one undisclosed AI teammate with an analytical, challenge-driven persona

participants.exclusions: No exclusions reported. The clustering analysis identifies 224 human speakers (p. 18). The N used in the creativity regression and the Kruskal-Wallis tests is not printed. Per-arm human counts are not printed; the group counts and composition (30x3, 33x2, 34x2) are stated on p. 7.
participants.who: University students (50.7% female) recruited via Prolific
participants.quote: A total of 224 university students (50.7% female) were recruited via Prolific to take part in an online small-group collaboration study.
participants.locator: p. 7, Section 3.1; p. 18, Section 4.3 ('291 speakers were identified (224 human, 67 AI)')

ai_tool.name_model: GPT-5-based generative models with persona system prompts (Appendix B)
ai_tool.how_used: The AI posed as a human teammate in the 10-minute group chat, never disclosing it was AI; it scanned the chat about every 25 seconds and posted with 50% probability, at most three consecutive turns. Participants did not use the AI directly, and it was absent when they wrote the individual post-task synopsis (p. 8-9, Sections 3.2-3.3).

task.description: Sci-fi movie plot in which AGI plays a central role, beginning 'In the year 2045, the world's first AGI unexpectedly...'; individual 50-100 word synopsis, then a triad chat to outline a plot, then an individual revised synopsis (Appendix A p. 28; p. 7-8)
task.duration: 10-minute group chat; duration of the individual writing phases not stated

outcomes.name: Creative performance change (Divergent Semantic Integration, post minus pre)
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Divergent Semantic Integration (DSI; Johnson et al., 2023), an embedding-based measure of semantic expansiveness of each person's 50-100 word synopsis; DSI scores were standardised and differenced (post minus pre) to give a change score; in the OLS model all continuous variables were rescaled to [0, 1] (p. 10 Section 3.5, Table 2; p. 13 Section 3.9)
outcomes.delay: Post-task synopsis written right after the 10-minute chat, without access to the chat logs or the baseline text

contrasts.reported: Kruskal-Wallis omnibus across the three conditions: condition did not significantly affect creative performance gains ('all p > .05'). OLS creative change ~ C(cluster) + C(condition), HC3 SEs: overall model F = 1.20, p = .310, R2 = .029; 'not predicted by either cluster or condition'. No condition coefficient, arm means, or SDs printed.

Same omnibus results: Kruskal-Wallis 'all p > .05' for creative performance gains; OLS overall model F = 1.20, p = .310, R2 = .029. No pairwise statistic, condition coefficient, arm means, or SDs printed.

eligibility.reason: Triads were randomized to a human-only control or to a triad with an undisclosed generative-AI teammate (supportive or contrarian) on a creative movie-plot task (p. 7). 224 students were randomized (p. 1, p. 7) and 224 humans appear in the analysis (p. 18), though the N in the creativity tests is not printed. Creativity is a computed DSI score on each person's own synopsis written after the chat, so the outcome answers after_ai (p. 8, p. 10). Caveats: assignment is clustered by triad; the AI is an undisclosed teammate rather than an assistant the person uses; only omnibus test results are printed for the creativity outcome.

one_line_finding: Neither a supportive nor a contrarian undisclosed AI teammate changed the DSI creativity of the synopsis each student wrote alone after the chat (Kruskal-Wallis all p > .05, p. 18; OLS F = 1.20, p = .310, R2 = .029, p. 19).
open_questions: Comparison type for AI arms versus control: coded ai_vs_active because the control triad has a third human where the AI arms have an AI teammate; it could instead be read as ai_vs_bau.
Whether an undisclosed AI teammate in a group chat counts as 'AI assistance' under criterion 1.
The N used in the creativity analyses and per-arm human counts are not printed; group composition implies 90, 66, and 68 humans but the paper does not state these numbers.
No arm means, SDs, or condition coefficients are printed for the creativity outcome; a standardized effect would require data from the authors.
notes: Other outcomes are discourse transition probabilities, sequential motifs, and clusters of chat utterances (process measures, not creativity scored on an output), and self-reported cognitive load, teamwork satisfaction, and psychological safety; none is listed as an outcome. The group plot outline produced during the chat (with AI present) was not scored. Pilot human-likeness rating (N = 15) and AI-detection rates (Supportive 25.5%, Contrarian 31.6%) on p. 9.
